title: Jeremiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 23
description: Ten questions on Jeremiah 23: the woe on the shepherds, the righteous Branch, and the long word against the lying prophets.

questions.text: On whom does the chapter open with a woe?
questions.explanation: Yahweh says, "Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!" and tells them He will visit on them the evil of their doings.

answers.text: On the kings of the nations around
On the craftsmen and the smiths of the city
On the elders of the land of Judah
On the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep

questions.text: What did Yahweh promise to do with the remnant of His flock?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said He would gather the remnant of his flock out of all the countries where He had driven them and bring them again to their folds, and they would be fruitful and multiply.

answers.text: Leave them among all the nations for ever and ever
Gather them out of all the countries and bring them back to their folds
Give them over to other shepherds to be sold
Scatter them even further, to the distant islands

questions.text: By what name would the righteous Branch raised to David be called?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said He would raise to David a righteous Branch who would reign as king, and that this is the name by which he will be called: Yahweh our righteousness.

answers.text: Yahweh our righteousness
Yahweh of Armies
The shepherd of Israel
Magormissabib

questions.text: How did the speaker describe himself when he spoke concerning the prophets?
questions.explanation: He said his heart within him was broken and all his bones shook, and that he was like a drunken man, like a man whom wine has overcome, because of Yahweh and his holy words.

answers.text: Like a watchman on the hills
Like a woman in travail with child
Like a drunken man whom wine has overcome
Like an untrained calf in the field

questions.text: To which two cities did Yahweh compare the prophets of Jerusalem and the city's inhabitants?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said that they had all become to him as Sodom, and its inhabitants as Gomorrah.

answers.text: Samaria and Shiloh
Tyre and Sidon
Ashkelon and Gaza
Sodom and Gomorrah

questions.text: What did Yahweh of Armies say He would feed the prophets with?
questions.explanation: Yahweh of Armies said concerning the prophets, "Behold, I will feed them with wormwood, and make them drink poisoned water."

answers.text: Straw and chaff from the floor
Wormwood, and poisoned water to drink
Sour grapes and bitter herbs
The bread of affliction

questions.text: What did those prophets keep telling the people who despised Yahweh?
questions.explanation: They said continually to those who despise him, "Yahweh has said, 'You will have peace,'" and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart, "No evil will come on you."

answers.text: That they would have peace and that no evil would come on them
That the sword and the famine were near
That they must serve the king of Babylon
That the city would be like Shiloh

questions.text: What did the prophets who prophesied lies in Yahweh's name keep saying?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said He had heard what the prophets said who prophesy lies in his name, saying, "I had a dream! I had a dream!"

answers.text: "Violence and destruction!"
"We are the shepherds of the flock!"
"I had a dream! I had a dream!"
"Who would come down against us?"

questions.text: To what two things did Yahweh compare His own word?
questions.explanation: Yahweh asked, "Isn't my word like fire? and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces?"

answers.text: To fire and to a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces
To the rain and to the dew on the grass
To a sword and to a bow of the mighty
To the wheat and to the straw

questions.text: What did Yahweh say at the end of the chapter that He would bring on them?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said, "I will bring an everlasting reproach on you, and a perpetual shame, which will not be forgotten."

answers.text: A famine of seven years
An everlasting reproach and a perpetual shame
A yoke of iron on their necks
A storm from the uttermost parts of the earth
